lead: Anaheim has 1950s and 1960s tract homes in the flats and hillside homes in Anaheim Hills. Aging plumbing, winter storms and hillside runoff drive water damage here.
risk: aging mid-century plumbing, hillside runoff and winter storm leaks
why: About 65% of Anaheim homes were built before 1980. In the flats of West Anaheim and The Colony, many tract homes still have galvanized steel or early copper supply lines and cast-iron drains. Galvanized pipe rusts from the inside, and old drains crack under the slab. Leaks often show up as warped floors, musty closets or a sewer smell after rain.

Anaheim Hills brings different risks. Homes sit on graded slopes, so heavy winter rain sends runoff toward foundations and patios. The hills have a history of ground movement; a January 1993 landslide destroyed more than 30 homes there. Most storms cause smaller problems, like water pushing under doors or through roof flashing. Southern California roofs also go months without rain, so leaks surprise owners with the first storm.
image_alt: Red house and a camper trailer surrounded by floodwater among bare trees
image_caption: Winter storms send runoff toward Anaheim homes, especially on hillside lots.
problems: Older homes in The Colony and the flats
tips: Ask a plumber whether your home still has galvanized supply pipe.
Have old cast-iron drains scoped with a camera.
Keep hillside drains and swales clear before winter.
Check your roof and flashing each fall, before the first big storm.
areas: Calls come from Anaheim Hills, The Colony, West Anaheim, the Platinum Triangle, the Anaheim Resort area, Downtown and East Anaheim, plus Fullerton, Orange and Yorba Linda.

faq.q: Does home insurance cover water damage from a landslide in Anaheim Hills?
faq.a: Usually not. Standard policies exclude earth movement, including landslides. Water damage from a sudden pipe burst is usually covered. If your home sits on a slope, ask your agent what is excluded and whether any extra coverage is available.
